title: Merged complex outputs and an annealed bit pair module on paired cubes: conditional κ = 5.878747e-4
body:
## Conditional improvement

$$T(n)=O\big(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\big),\qquad \kappa=\frac{5878747}{10^{10}}=5.878747\times10^{-4}.$$

This is **+27.54% over #144** (4.609169e-4, merged), +5.83% over #157 (5.555021e-4), which it supersedes, and +4.67% over #160 (5.616446e-4). The complex side binds: its saving is 5885669/10¹⁰, while the bit coarse saving is 5936323/10¹⁰. All of #144's interfaces remain assumptions.

## Change

This is #157 with three changes: merged complex outputs on a new annealed pair module, an annealed bit pair module, and phase stop β = 10⁻⁹.

| side | word | R | W per vertex | saving |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| complex | #157 | 17,529 | 16,539 | 5622769/10¹⁰ |
| complex | **this** | **16,011** | **15,681** | **5885669/10¹⁰** |
| bit | #157 (witness-cut module) | 25,624 | 29,144 | 5566382/10¹⁰ (coarse) |
| bit | **this** | **23,368** | **26,888** | **5936323/10¹⁰ (coarse)** |

- **Complex: #144's paired cubes at p = 11 (h = 22), with physical frames and late-read reuse.**
  - The triple module is the same exact restriction of a pinned searched complex DAG as in #157. The pair module is a new pinned, annealed pair-disjoint module (365 additions), with its contract checked on load. Both are in `references/paired-cube/sources`.
  - **Output merging.** For every port T = (I, b), the face-2 output P and the edge-02 output Q are replaced by one signed node P + (2b₀ − 1)Q per (b₀, b₂), read with coefficient 1/2 by both ports b₁ = 0, 1 (`merge_outputs` in `scripts/paired_cube/modules.py`). The decoder contribution is unchanged and every addition keeps disjoint supports.
  - The carrier arcs are frozen: R = 16,011, with 2,970 rank-18 gauges.
  - `scripts/paired_cube_physical.py` moves 7,880 operation frames by physical descent (#131's method under #130's Clifford frames). It places every gauged role in a dead donor's slot (#124), with the old-value read immediately before the role's first operation (#143).
  - Per vertex: W = 15,681, deficit 1,320, largest child 20.
- **Bit: the paired-cube bit word in `research/paired-cube-bit`** (p = 12; partner-pair source mixing per `LEMMA.md`), now with an annealed pair-disjoint module (438 additions) in `data/pair_module_p12.json`.
  - The witness-cut module is kept as `data/pair_module_p12_cut.json`, and `derive_pair_modules.py` still regenerates it.
  - The carrier matching is re-solved and frozen in `data/arcs_p12.json`.
  - #160 also uses a searched pair module in the bit word, at p = 11. This PR keeps p = 12 with a separately annealed module.
- **Phase stop β = 10⁻⁹** (was 10⁻⁶), as re-instantiated by @geckods (#153, #158).

#144's checks, finite bridge, row reserve and assembly are otherwise unchanged.

## Verification

```sh
make paired-cube-verify
python3 research/paired-cube-bit/paired_cube_bit_word.py --p 12 --check
python3 research/paired-cube-bit/check_paired_cube_bit.py --dir research/paired-cube-bit/out --p 12
```

- **Producer.** It regenerates the complex input and passes all of #144's independent checks.
- **Physical layer.** It checks:
  - value spans and nested role chains, with every handoff spliced;
  - pair chronology;
  - target chains in actual read order;
  - the telescoping deficit;
  - an exact aliased dirty-scratch replay mod 2⁶¹ − 1, with three controls rejected.
- **Bit checker.** It recomputes the exact frames, the decoder identity, the chains, the partner-pair chronology, nondegeneracy, an F2 replay and the ledger, and five mutation controls are rejected. The generator regenerates the word and profile identically from the frozen arcs.
- **Assembly.** Both moments are strict, with the next grid points rejected. All 47 constraints and 7 margins hold.
- Every command above passes on Linux with a clean working tree, as do the maintainer's paired-cube entry-point tests and the full `make verify`.
